sentences.text:
The present bail application has been filed under Section 439 of
Cr.P.C. on behalf of the petitioner, who is in custody in connection with F.I.R. No.75/2019, Police
Station Dhorimana, District Barmer for the offence under Sections 8/15, 29 of Ndps Act, 3/25 of
Arms Act and 420, 468 and 471 of Ipc.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the co- accused Ranaram and Maniya @ Manohar have been enlarged on bail by this Court.
He further submits that except the statement of co-accused Ranaram, there is no evidence on record to connect the present petitioner with the recovery of contraband in the present case.

He further submits that the petitioner has already [2024:RJ-JD:51225] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-10423/2023] suffered incarceration for almost two years and,
therefore, he may be enlarged on bail.
Per contra

, learned Public Prosecutor submits that the petitioner was travelling in the vehicle from which the contraband was recovered and on seeing the raiding party, the petitioner along with Ranaram tried to flee from the spot.

However, Ranaram was nabbed on the spot and immediately,

sentences.text: on being nabbed, Ranaram disclosed that the person who fled from the place was Chokha Ram.
Learned Public Prosecutor further submits that there are two more NDPS cases are registered against the present petitioner for which he is facing trial.
He further submits that huge quantity of contraband (395 Kgs of Poppy Husk) has been recovered from the vehicle in which the petitioner was travelling.
He, therefore, prays that the bail application of the petitioner may be rejected.
I have considered the submissions made at the bar and have gone through the relevant record of the case.
The fact that the petitioner was travelling in the car has come on record in the statement of Seizure Officer, whose statement has been recorded before the trial Court as PW-2.
Even in the statement of Ranaram, immediately after being nabbed, he has disclosed the name of the present petitioner.
It is further noted that against the present petitioner, two more cases of NDPS are registered against him at different police stations and he is facing trial for the same.
In the present case, 395 Kgs of Poppy Husk has been recovered, which is a huge quantity.

Considering the overall circumstances, prima facie, this Court is of the view that the petitioner is habitually involved in the NDPS [2024:RJ-JD:51225] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-10423/2023] cases and taking into consideration the huge quantity of contraband recovered in the present case and the case of the present petitioner is not standing on similar footings to the case of Ranaram, who has suffered incarceration for more than four years, this Court is not inclined to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. to the petitioner at this stage.
Accordingly, the present bail application preferred by the petitioner under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.

(VINIT KUMAR MATHUR),J 525-Shahenshah/-
